subject: Sampling weights with TMB random effects models

messages.author: 402856652ba9dda3
messages.subject: Sampling weights with TMB random effects models
parts:
I came across this thread, where Skaug noted that using a weighted loglikelihood creates problems with the Laplace approximation.

From my understanding (I was a little lost with the context), the proposed solution was to create a function in R that loops over the rows, calls MakeADFun for each individual, then weights the result.  Then simply call optim on this wrapping function.

The issue here though, is that this seems like it would drastically increase computation time.  Is there not a more performative way to go about this?

messages.author: 02e03030784aa6a7
messages.subject: Re: Sampling weights with TMB random effects models
parts:
What you suggest would of course work, but would be extremely inefficient. My idea 
was to call  MakeADFun  once to get the incorrectly weighted marginal likelihood, and then
obtain the correction by some other means. Exactly how to do the latter part needs a bit more thought.

Hans

messages.subject: Re: Sampling weights with TMB random effects models
parts:
Ultimately I decided that the best way to go about this is probably to do the Laplace approximation manually (à la laplace.cpp), and weight it post-hoc within the C++ objective.

Thanks for the response,
Josh Pritsker
